name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.1% a year in October, up for a third month and inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band
state: FRED data put annual US CPI inflation at 4.08% in October, up from 4.02% in September and rising for a third consecutive month, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band. Inflation has risen from about 2.7% in February as energy prices climbed. The November CPI report is due in mid-December.
for_you: Rising prices squeeze real incomes, especially for households with large fuel and food budgets. Borrowers on variable rates are exposed if the Federal Reserve raises rates further.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.08% within 3.0–4.5% Watch band; rising 3 months
why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
